h: Tunnel Tips and a Day Out in North Hampshire
p: Your first flight is a funny mix of noise, wind and sheer excitement, and it's over before you know it. To make the most of it, keep your body loose rather than stiff, look up and ahead rather than down, and keep an eye on the instructor's hand signals. They're there to help you, so don't worry about getting everything perfect straight away.

Prep is easy but important. Empty your pockets, remove jewellery and watches, wear trainers that lace up, and tie long hair back. If you wear glasses or contact lenses, tell the team when you check in. Arrive early for the briefing and keep big meals for after your flight. Families should check the guidelines for younger flyers before booking.
Spectators can watch from outside the tunnel, so bring someone along to cheer you on. Lots of flyers also opt for a photo or video, so you can prove to the doubters that you really did fly.

Basingstoke makes a cracking base for exploring North Hampshire. The Vyne, a National Trust house with gardens and woodland walks, lies just north of town, and the Basingstoke Canal is perfect for a peaceful towpath stroll. Jane Austen fans can head to Chawton, where Jane Austen's House is set in the village where she spent her last years, and the cathedral city of Winchester is an easy drive away. Back in town, the Anvil is the place to go for concerts and shows.
